channel.title: Clisa Geopolitics
channel.description: A geopolitical dashboard analyzing Northeast Asian security, great-power competition, and conflicts in Europe and the Middle East from South Korea’s vantage point. Each issue comes with a situation assessment, a strategy evaluation, what it means for people, and probabilistic forecasts.

item.title: Features · Why North Korea is holding off on ICBM test launches
item.description: The fifth feature, “Why North Korea is holding off on ICBM test launches,” is now up. It looks at why North Korea is holding off on testing ICBMs built to reach the U.S. mainland while it keeps testing missiles built to strike South Korea and Japan, and at the risk that choice leaves South Korea facing.

item.title: Method change · The economic measure now tracks income loss rather than income level
item.description: We changed the economic measure in Impact on people from income level to income loss, so that shocks that sharply reduce income, such as South Korea's 1998 financial crisis, show up properly in the scores. As a result, 29 classifications changed, including that of South Koreans in a blockade of Taiwan.

item.title: Features · The Russia-Ukraine war: why the attrition goes on
item.description: The fourth feature, “The Russia-Ukraine war: why the attrition goes on,” uses People's Lives data to show how Russia keeps the war's impact confined to the front while Ukrainian society as a whole wears down, and identifies what could change that dynamic.

item.title: Issues · Russia-Ukraine war: U.S. waives Russia sanctions; top-ranked combination stands
item.description: President Trump's October 16 executive order waived most of the tariffs and sanctions in the Graham Russia sanctions law, meeting a warning signal in the Russia-Ukraine analysis: the United States lifting tariffs on buyers of Russian oil. The order cited only the national interest, but it came a week after a deal to import Russian diesel, and Trump has pointed to diesel prices ahead of the midterm elections. Washington has demanded that Ukraine stop striking Russian refineries and has even suggested Ukraine needs a new president, but no U.S. demand for territorial concessions has been confirmed, and Europe has kept its line of increasing pressure on Russia. The top-ranked combination—a self-sufficient defense industry and a ceasefire that does not legally cede occupied territory—therefore stands. With Washington setting aside its means of pressing Russia, however, the burden of guaranteeing a ceasefire has shifted further toward Europe.

item.title: Features · What it took for a country to invent an alphabet
item.description: A third feature, "What it took for a country to invent an alphabet," was published for Hangul Day. It traces the two conditions, one domestic and one external, that sustained King Sejong's 32-year reign: where they came from and why they lasted only a generation. It then puts the same question to the Korean Peninsula of 2026.
